title: Perfect maps on an open lift with support
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], let U\subset X be a quasi-compact open, and let T\subset X be a closed subset with X\setminus T quasi-compact. Let E be an object of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] and let \alpha:P\to E|_U be a morphism, where P is a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_U) [def-pc-perfect-complex] supported on T\cap U. Then there are a perfect object R of D(\mathcal O_X) supported on T and a morphism \beta:R\to E such that P is a direct summand of R|_U in D(\mathcal O_U), compatibly with \alpha and \beta|_U.

proof.text: Use the finite affine-cover stabilized construction on the recursively defined S(0)=P and S(k+1)=S(k) plus S(k)[1], with a(0)=alpha and a(k+1)=first projection followed by a(k). It gives n, R, beta, perfectness, support and an isomorphism e: R|U ≅ S(n) satisfying beta|U=e followed by a(n).

Prove by induction on n that P is a compatible summand of S(n). At zero take the identity. At the successor compose the old inclusion with biproduct inclusion, and compose biproduct projection with the old projection. The equation inl followed by fst = identity proves the retraction equation and compatibility with a(n). This is stabilization_split in Lean, using Mathlib biprod.inl_fst_assoc.

Compose the inclusion into S(n) with e inverse and compose e with the projection from S(n). The iso inverse-hom identity proves the retraction equation. Substitution of the construction map equation followed by the same iso identity proves compatibility with alpha.

proof_origin.note: The original finite affine attachment route is retained in the new construction node. The categorical summand induction and iso transport are complete Lean proofs.
